'''Thomas F. Stocker''' (born 1959) is a Swiss [[climate scientist]].

Born in Zürich, Stocker obtained a degree in physics at the [[ETH Zurich]]. He was active in research at the [[University College London]], at [[McGill University]] in Montreal and at [[Columbia University]] in New York. Since 1993, he has been a professor and head of the department of [[Environmental science|Climate and Environmental Physics]] at the [[University of Bern]].<ref name="NZZ 1 November 2013">{{cite news|last=Hofmann|first=Markus|title=Klimawissenschafter Thomas Stocker: Der Klimaforscher mit der dicken Haut|url=http://www.nzz.ch/aktuell/schweiz/der-klimaforscher-mit-der-dicken-haut-1.18177242|accessdate=1 November 2013|newspaper=[[Neue Zürcher Zeitung]]|date=1 November 2013}}</ref>

The focus of Stocker's research is the development of models of [[climate change]] based on, among other, the analysis of [[ice core]]s from the polar regions. He significantly contributed to creating the "[[hockey stick graph (global temperature)|hockey stick graph]]" that shows a growing increase of global mean temperatures in recent times. Since 1998, he contributes to the reports of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]], and is co-chairman of the IPCC Working Group I (assessing scientific aspects of the climate system and climate change) from 2008 to 2015.<ref name="NZZ 1 November 2013" />

In 1993, Stocker was awarded the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]]'s National Latsis Prize,<ref name=Latzis/> in 2009 the [[Hans Oeschger Medal]] of the [[European Geosciences Union]] and in 2017 the [[Marcel Benoist Prize]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Top Swiss science prize gets boost |url=https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/marcel-benoist-prize_top-swiss-science-prize-gets-boost/43639544 |accessdate=28 October 2018 |agency=SwissInfo |publisher=SwissInfo |date=31 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Swiss Science Prize Marcel Benoist |url=https://marcel-benoist.ch/en/ |website=marcel-benoist.ch |accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref> For 2023 he received the [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award]].<ref>[https://www.frontiersofknowledgeawards-fbbva.es/ BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award 2023]</ref>

He is a Fellow of the [[American Geophysical Union]] and a member of the [[Academia Europaea]]. In 2019, Stocker became a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web |title= Thomas Stocker |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/thomas-f-stocker/|publisher=German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina |access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref>

Stocker is featured in the film ''Taking Earth's Temperature: Delving into Climate's Past''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://takingearthstemperature.org/ |title=Taking Earth's Temperature &#124; Delving into Climate's Past |access-date=2014-10-31 |archive-date=2014-10-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141031061629/http://takingearthstemperature.org/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
